items.title: Roy Palmer Interview, 1955-09-22
items.q: One fellow's named George Williams. He's one of the best supposed to be. He said that, I said that he was a better trombone player than I am, but he said I was better than him.

ctx.x: When you started, you started right on the trombone, was it very interesting? Yeah, on the trombone. How did you happen to like that better than others?

I don't know, I take my liking to trombone. There was a show that came into New Orleans, and they had two trombones. And I noticed a fellow that was playing trombone. He was quick and fast, and he could handle that trombone faster. Well, when I first started, I told fellows I was going to imitate that fellow. And they tried to disgust me. They said, you'll never play like that fellow. They said, you'll never play like that fellow. I said, well, I don't know, I'm going to try. And I kept trying and doing it wrong.…
There was one of George Williams that played in Handy up in Memphis.
